name: manual_a20c04
claim: A test that only asserts the outer/observable outcome of a code path (e.g. 'accepted is False') can pass vacuously even when the specific mechanism it's meant to verify never actually fired (e.g. a reputation-penalty call, a lock acquisition, a cache write). When adding a test for 'X happened as a side effect of Y', assert on X's own state directly (the ledger's score moved, the cache has an entry, the lock's internal counter changed) — not just that Y's return value looks plausible, which can be true for reasons unrelated to X.
conditions: vacuous test pass precondition assertion side effect verification mock produces expected state before checking downstream effect

decisions.notes: 2026-07-11: caught this in my own draft test twice this session. First: a Sybil risk-scoring test asserted 'if risk == high: check accepted' without first asserting risk actually WAS high — the mocked is_correlated=True didn't produce high risk due to a real off-by-one in the threshold math (len(correlated) > len(witness_ids)/2 is unreachable at 2 witnesses when only one side of each pair is recorded), and the test passed vacuously until I added an explicit precondition assertion, which then failed and revealed the real bug. Second: when adding a reputation-feedback test, asserted ledger.reputation_weight() actually moved, not just that the pipeline's own accepted/decision_type outcome looked right.
